Rank values, in parallel

Source: R/par-rank.R
par_rank.Rd

Returns the same as base rank(), but sorts the values on several threads. Base rank() is slow where values tie: it takes seconds for a million doubles.

Usage

par_rank(
  x,
  na.last = TRUE,
  ties.method = c("average", "first", "last", "random", "max", "min"),
  nthreads = getOption("parvenu.threads", 0L)
)

Arguments

x

a numeric, complex, character or logical vector.

na.last

a logical or character string controlling the treatment of NAs. If TRUE, missing values in the data are put last; if FALSE, they are put first; if NA, they are removed; if "keep" they are kept with rank NA.

ties.method

a character string specifying how ties are treated, see ‘Details’; can be abbreviated.

nthreads

A whole number: the max number of threads to use. 0 means the RAYON_NUM_THREADS environment variable, or else all cores. The default is the parvenu.threads option, or 0 if that isn't set. Inputs too small to keep that many threads busy get fewer, and more threads than cores count as all cores.

Value

As rank(): the ranks, a double vector for "average" and an integer one otherwise, with the names of x.

Details

Computed in Rust for integer and double vectors and factors of at least 1e4 elements. Anything else goes to base R. So does ties.method = "random", which draws random numbers.

Examples

x <- c(b = 3, a = 1, c = 3, d = NA)
par_rank(x)
#>   b   a   c   d 
#> 2.5 1.0 2.5 4.0 
par_rank(x, ties.method = "min", na.last = "keep")
#>  b  a  c  d 
#>  2  1  2 NA
